newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TENNIS-CHANG LIFTS HONG KONG SALEM OPEN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG LIFTS HONG KONG SALEM OPEN TITLE.

text.p: Top seed Michael Chang of the United States took just 45 seconds to finish off the rain-delayed final of the Hong Kong Salem Open against Australia's Patrick Rafter on Monday.
Chang led 6-3 5-3 and had two match points on his serve in hand overnight after a heavy shower halted play on Sunday.
The fifth-seeded Rafter won the first point when the final resumed with an overhead smash but then hit a backhand long on the next point to give Chang a 6-3 6-3 victory.

ATP Tour officials on site said they could not recall another occasion a final has been delayed overnight by rain with a player holding match point. In all, the match took 19 hours and 52 minutes to complete.
Chang, a winner in Memphis and Indian Wells earlier this year, gained the upper hand on Sunday with a great display of baseline tennis.

"I do not know how many times I thought about the match last night," said Chang, who also won here in 1994 and 1995. "There were so many things going through my mind -- should I hit it to his backhand, should I slice it or serve and volley.
"It is strange to have so much time to think about a match, especially when the first few points are so important. If I lost them it could have been a turning point in the whole match."
Chang said he relaxed in the early hours of Monday morning by watching television coverage of compatriot Tiger Woods on his way to a record victory in the U.S. Masters golf championship.

"He is quite incredible -- it made me think a bit about me winning the French Open at 17 and how professionals accomplish things so young. I had the feeling Tiger Woods did not quite know what was going on and it was like that for me at the French. It was only afterwards that I realised the significance," said Chang, winner of the French Open in 1989.
Rafter said that he tried to be calm when play resumed.
"I just tried to be relaxed but it was over quickly," said Rafter, the world number 43. "I had my chances yesterday but did not take them. He took his chances and that is why he is where he is."
